The sign of the remainder can show whether an approximation is high or low. Use a valid
derivative bound over the entire interval, not just at the center. Degree and number of nonzero
terms differ: a sine polynomial of degree five has three nonzero terms. A sufficient upper bound
exceeding a tolerance does not prove that the true error exceeds it; minimum-term questions
need a lower bound or a direct remainder argument as well.
The finite Taylor theorem does not require the infinite Taylor series to converge at the evalua-
tion point: it needs the stated differentiability on the intervening interval. Combining Taylor
expansions at symmetric points can cancel odd powers and yield derivative-approximation
bounds.
